answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to cultivate a unique opal-linked reputation trellis: peers only stake meaningful value after observing consistent behavior over multiple epochs. An attacker spawning many fakes must either wait long for each to reach the summit of trusted status or pay for artificial interactions, which peers can detect and slash, multiplying the cost linearly with the number of identities while honest agents pay only normal participation fees.
